title: KV prefetch stream-lag causing slab orphaning and slow resident growth
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Under sustained continuous-batching workloads with aggressive KV prefetching, we observe slow, persistent GPU resident-memory growth that does not plateau. Growth appears as small, scattered allocations that never get coalesced back into arena free lists (we're calling this 'slab orphaning'). Hypothesis: KV prefetch tasks allocate pinned/staging buffers and small device buffers across many streams; due to stream-lag on frees (deferred-free until stream completion) plus cudaMallocAsync pooling behavior we keep creating micro-slab fragments that the pool never reclaims. This is distinct from a single large leak — it's a slow slope caused by accumulation of tiny allocations that escape compaction heuristics.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 nightly to a 4xA100 pool with default cudaMallocAsync pool enabled
2) Run kv-prefetch-heavy benchmark (tooling: internal loadgen kv-prefetch v2) at 500-700 rps with batch sizes 1-4 for 6+ hours
3) Monitor nvidia-smi and /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/memory; collect per-process resident and tracked pool stats every minute
4) Capture nvprof/nvtx traces for 30s slices during growth window and record stream_event latency histograms
5) Repeat with cudaMallocAsync disabled (fallback to cudaMalloc) as control and with a single-stream prefetch path as additional control.
investigation_notes: Observed slope: resident +3.9 MB/hour on baseline runs; after a quick heap warmup resident plateaus only when load drops. Under steady load the slope persists.

nvtx traces show many small allocations on distinct streams with free calls returning quickly but cudaMemPool calls not merging because stream completion fences are delayed ~200-400ms for certain prefetch tasks.

Pool metrics: high small-allocation churn (4-32KB allocations) with >60% of them in 'staging/pinned' bucket. Pool fragmentation metric shows many <64KB free chunks that are isolated by stream affinity.

Kernel timeline: KV prefetch does async host->device memcpy on per-request streams; request completion triggers eviction path which queues cudaFree on same stream but we observed a race where stream is reused before pool can reuse freed segments leading to transient resident bumps.
Control run (cudaMallocAsync disabled) reduced slope to +0.5 MB/hour but increased per-allocation latency by ~15%. Indicates pooling behavior is implicated in the leak pattern.

Reproducer: small internal harness that repeatedly prefetches random KV slices recreated the slope within 90 minutes on a local dev A100; enabling a forced cudaStreamSynchronize() before free eliminated slope in harness, confirming deferred-free latency interaction.
proposed_changes: A) Short-term mitigation: add a 'prefetch stream affinity' flag that runs KV prefetches on a bounded set of dedicated streams so freed staging memory is more likely to be coalesced before stream reuse. Experimented in branch ENG/218210/affinity - reduced slope to +0.9 MB/hour.

B) Medium-term: implement a deferred-free coalescer thread that batch-processes pending frees from multiple streams and issues coalescing hints to cudaMemPool (or issues synchronous fences in safe windows). Adds a configurable budget to avoid tail-latency regressions.

C) Heuristic eviction: when small-chunk fragmentation grows beyond threshold, trigger background arena compaction that migrates hot KV slices into reserved contiguous arenas and releases orphaned slabs to the OS/pool.
D) Disable small-pool fast-path for allocations < 64KB when they are coming from KV prefetch path (configurable); forces them into a separate pool that has more aggressive compaction policies.
E) Add observability: track per-stream allocate/free histograms and expose 'orphaned slab' gauge to Console. Create alert when slope > 1 MB/hour for 3h on dedicated instances.
experiments: affinity-flag run (24h): slope reduced from +3.9 to +0.9 MB/hr; CPU overhead +1%
forced-sync patch (dev only): slope -> 0 MB/hr but tail p95 latency regressed 12% — unacceptable for PLG tier
separate-pool-for-small-allocs prototype: slope -> +0.4 MB/hr; increases fragmentation metric but allows background compaction to reclaim chunks more effectively
deferred-free-coalescer simulation: expected to reduce slope to near-zero with <2% p99 latency impact when tuned; further validation required on mixed workloads
decision: Landing plan: ship affinity-flag as opt-in in runtime-1.20 to mitigate customer impact while we stabilize deferred-free-coalescer in runtime-1.21. Metric gates required before turning on by default.
Follow-ups: implement Console charts and alerting, schedule load tests across Dedicated fleet in Cycle 42, and open RFC for allocator compaction primitives.
